applicableAreas: Buildings 6, 7, and 8 (closest to OHE line on southern boundary)
findings.comment: Buildings maintain minimum 20-30 feet horizontal clearance from overhead electric line on southern boundary, exceeding the 7.5-foot minimum requirement.

agentTrace.observation: Vision measurement of site plan (Sheet 9) shows Buildings 6, 7, and 8 are positioned 20.7 to 27.3 feet from the OHE line running along the southern property boundary.
agentTrace.reasoning: The measured horizontal distances of 20-30 feet are substantially greater than the required 7.5-foot minimum sky-to-ground clearance. Compliance can be confirmed from the plan geometry without additional annotations.

applicableAreas: Electrical transformers and customer facilities on site
findings.comment: Electrical design plan shows transformers and meter locations but contains no dimension lines or clearance annotations demonstrating the 15-foot radial clearance requirement from the outside conductor of overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Unable to determine if 15-foot radial clearance is maintained.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) depicts electrical transformer pads and meters with text labels but lacks any dimension lines showing distances from the overhead electric line to these customer facilities.
agentTrace.reasoning: Without explicit clearance dimensions or geometric reference points showing distances from the OHE conductor to the transformers/meters, compliance cannot be verified. The plan shows facilities and the general location of the overhead line but provides no measurable evidence of clearance distances.

findings.comment: No building elevation sheets showing building projections (overhangs, awnings, balconies) with clearance dimensions to the overhead electric conductor are included in the submittal. Roofs and overhangs are not dimensionally verified for compliance with the 7.5-foot sky-to-ground and 15-foot radial clearance requirements.

agentTrace.observation: Review of site plan sheets and building data tables shows building heights but no elevation views or projection details with clearance annotations to the overhead electric line.
agentTrace.reasoning: The applicability condition for this item (building projections extending toward overhead conductors) cannot be evaluated without architectural elevation drawings showing roof edges, overhangs, and their clearances from the OHE line. The absence of these sheets prevents compliance verification.

applicableAreas: Buildings 6, 7, and 8 adjacent to OHE line
findings.comment: No building elevation sheets are included in the submittal showing surveyed elevations and locations of the overhead electric conductor. Registered surveyor data for conductor elevations and mid-span clearances to building features is not provided.

agentTrace.observation: The site plan provides building heights (33'-4.75" to 36'-1") and benchmark elevations but no dedicated building elevation sheets with surveyed overhead conductor elevation data.
agentTrace.reasoning: Verification of vertical clearances requires surveyed conductor elevation information shown on building elevation drawings. Without surveyor-certified elevation data for the overhead line, the actual vertical clearance from buildings to the conductor cannot be determined.

applicableAreas: Buildings 6, 7, and 8 adjacent to OHE line on southern property boundary
findings.comment: Site plan and electrical design sheets do not contain dimension lines with annotations showing clearances from the outer electric conductor to the outermost edges of buildings and building projections. Although geometric measurement confirms buildings are positioned with adequate clearance, the required dimension exhibits for clearance verification are absent from the submitted plans.

agentTrace.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 site plan and Sheet 21 electrical plan reveals no visible dimension lines or numerical callouts (e.g., '25 ft min. clearance') between the OHE line and building edges.
agentTrace.reasoning: The code requirement specifically calls for dimension and section view exhibits showing clearance verification. While the buildings' geometric position provides adequate clearance, the applicant has not provided the specific dimension annotations required by UCM § 1.10.3 as an alternative to registered surveyor documentation.

applicableAreas: Concrete fence on southern property boundary; Sidewalk Easement fence on western property boundary
findings.comment: Concrete fence on southern boundary maintains approximately 14.4 feet clearance from OHE line; Sidewalk Easement fence on western boundary maintains approximately 47 feet clearance from OHE line. Both exceed the 7.5-foot minimum sky-to-ground clearance requirement.

agentTrace.observation: Vision measurement of Sheet 9 shows concrete fence (southern) at 14.4 feet from OHE line and Sidewalk Easement fence (northwestern corner) at 47 feet from OHE line.
agentTrace.reasoning: Both measured fence clearances (14.4' and 47') exceed the required 7.5-foot minimum, confirming compliance with the horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement.

findings.comment: Fence locations shown on site plan do not conflict with overhead electric utility pole locations. Minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from fence posts to poles is maintained.

agentTrace.observation: Site plan shows fences positioned along property boundaries with utility poles marked at intervals; fences do not appear to intersect pole locations.
agentTrace.reasoning: The visible fence alignments on the site plan (southern boundary concrete fence, western boundary sidewalk fence) maintain adequate clearance from the utility pole symbols shown on the plan.

applicableAreas: Concrete retaining wall on southern property boundary
findings.comment: Concrete retaining wall positioned along the southern property line is located only approximately 1 foot from the overhead electric line, far below the required 7.5-foot minimum horizontal sky-to-ground clearance. Wall must be relocated or OHE line must be relocated to achieve required clearance.

agentTrace.observation: Vision measurement of Sheet 9 site plan shows concrete retaining wall on southern boundary running parallel to the OHE line with only approximately 1 foot separation.
agentTrace.reasoning: The measured 1-foot clearance is approximately 7.5 times smaller than the code minimum of 7.5 feet. This represents a clear violation of the horizontal sky-to-ground clearance requirement. The wall is positioned directly adjacent to the overhead line conductor.

applicableAreas: Retaining wall on southern property boundary near OHE line
findings.comment: Retaining wall detail sheets (Sheet 38 - Wall Plan) and site plan (Sheet 9) do not include section views with dimension annotations showing the clearance from the outer electric conductor to the outermost face of the retaining wall. Required cross-sectional exhibits for clearance verification are absent.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 38 contains retaining wall structural details but no sections showing the wall's relationship to the overhead electric line or clearance dimensions. Sheet 9 site plan shows the wall position but without dimension callouts to the OHE line.
agentTrace.reasoning: The code requires section exhibits with dimensions demonstrating required clearances. The wall plan provides structural details but does not address the clearance conflict with the adjacent overhead electric facility.

applicableAreas: Driveway entrance on southern property (Type III driveway crossing OHE line)
findings.comment: Site plan shows a driveway (29 feet wide) crossing under the overhead electric line on the southern property boundary, but no section or profile views are provided showing the vertical clearance from the lowest point of the overhead electric conductor to the finished driveway grade. Cannot verify compliance with the 16-foot (parking without truck traffic) or 18-foot (areas with truck traffic) minimum vertical clearance requirement. No mid-span clearance survey data provided.

agentTrace.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirms an OHE line crosses the main entrance driveway (labeled 'Construct Type III Driveway, See Detail 433S-2'). Sheet 22 contains standard driveway detail 433S-2 but shows only structural/pavement requirements, not vertical clearance from overhead lines. No elevation views are provided.
agentTrace.reasoning: Vertical clearance verification requires either surveyed conductor elevation data or section/profile views showing the OHE line height and finished driveway elevation. Neither is provided in the submittal. The reference to standard detail 433S-2 addresses only pavement construction, not overhead utility clearances.

applicableAreas: All clearance dimensions on site plan and electrical sheets
findings.comment: No clearance dimension callouts are shown on the submitted plans. Therefore, cannot verify whether any dimension lines originate from the outside conductor (as required) or from the utility pole centerline. The critical measurement methodology requirement cannot be evaluated from the available plans.

agentTrace.observation: Review of Sheet 9 site plan and Sheet 21 electrical design plan shows no visible dimension lines annotating clearances between the OHE line and site features.
agentTrace.reasoning: Since no dimension callouts are provided on the plans, the measurement origin point (conductor vs. pole) cannot be verified. This prevents assessment of whether the applicant complied with the requirement to measure from the outside conductor rather than pole centerline.

applicableAreas: Retaining wall on eastern property boundary within 5-foot electric easement
findings.comment: Site plan shows an existing retaining wall marked 'to be replaced' located within or adjacent to a labeled '5' Electric Easement (Vol. 69, Pg. 14)' on the eastern property boundary. No clearance dimensions or verification exhibits confirm that the replacement wall will maintain the minimum 7.5-foot clearance from outside conductor or that it will not be installed under/over the overhead distribution facilities. Coordination with Austin Energy regarding easement usage and clearance requirements cannot be verified.

agentTrace.observation: Vision analysis of Sheet 9 shows an 'Existing Retaining Wall to be Replaced' with a leader line pointing to a location aligned with a labeled electric easement on the east property line. No clearance dimensions or coordination notes are provided.
agentTrace.reasoning: The plan indicates a wall replacement within or near an electric easement but provides no evidence of clearance verification or Austin Energy coordination. Without dimension callouts or notes confirming clearance compliance or easement authorization, the replacement wall's compliance with the prohibition on facilities under/over overhead distribution lines cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: Driveway and buildings adjacent to OHE line
findings.comment: No registered surveyor mid-span clearance data is provided showing pole locations, conductor elevations, and measured vertical clearances from overhead electric facilities to the driveway grade or building features. Survey data from a registered surveyor demonstrating whether vertical clearances meet minimums is absent from the submittal.

agentTrace.observation: Review of survey data references (Sheet 4 Existing Conditions Survey shows registered surveyor certification) and all subsequent sheets shows no surveyed conductor elevation data or mid-span clearance measurements.
agentTrace.reasoning: The code allows clearance verification via either registered surveyor data or engineered dimension exhibits on plans. The registered surveyor survey (CDS Survey, Project No. 18-03-0225:021) has documented property topography and existing conditions but does not include overhead conductor elevation data or clearance measurements. This critical documentation is absent.

applicableAreas: Trees and landscaping on southern and southeastern portion of site adjacent to OHE line
findings.comment: Mitigation trees (marked 'M' on landscape plan, Sheet 31) are proposed within 0.9 to 3.9 feet of the overhead electric distribution line on the southern boundary, all well within the 10-foot lateral clearance requirement for trees near overhead distribution conductors. Individual tree species for mitigation trees are not clearly identified on the landscape plan or cross-referenced to the plant list. Cannot confirm that all mitigation trees within the 10-foot zone are from the Utility Compatible Shade Trees list (ECM Appendix F, species marked 'UC'). The landscape plan plant list shows Live Oak, Cedar Elm, Texas Mountain Laurel, and Mexican Redbud, but the specific species of the mitigation trees positioned near the OHE line is not documented. Furthermore, standard landscaping practice requires that only utility-compatible species (typically mature height ≤20 feet, marked 'UC') be planted within this lateral distance zone.

agentTrace.observation: Vision measurement of Sheet 31 identifies mitigation trees labeled 'M' at distances of 0.9, 2.4, 2.4, and 3.9 feet from the OHE line. Cross-reference to Sheet 35 plant list shows proposed shade trees (Live Oak, Cedar Elm) and ornamental trees (Texas Mountain Laurel, Mexican Redbud), but the specific species of the mitigation trees near the OHE line are not designated on either the landscape plan or the plant list.
agentTrace.reasoning: The 0.9 to 3.9-foot spacing places all mitigation trees within the 10-foot required clearance zone for overhead distribution conductors. ECM § 2.4.1.D and § 2.4.2.C limit plantings in this zone to utility-compatible species. Without explicit species identification for these mitigation trees and confirmation of their utility-compatible status, compliance cannot be verified. Lack of species designation on the plan is itself a deficiency.

applicableAreas: General project site with overhead electric transmission lines
findings.comment: Cover sheet (Sheet 3) includes a note regarding 48-hour notification to Austin Energy before work near energized transmission lines (reference to Andrew Perez, 512-505-7153). However, the required note specified in UCM § 1.10.2 should address notification requirements for work near all high-voltage overhead lines (both distribution and transmission), not transmission lines exclusively. The current note is transmission-specific and does not clearly address the general 48-hour notification requirement for distribution facilities per the broader code language.

agentTrace.observation: Sheet 3 contains an 'Electric Transmission Notes' section with Note #3 requiring a pre-construction safety meeting with Austin Energy 48 hours before construction, specifically for work near 'energized transmission lines.' A separate 'Electric Notes' section references general responsibility for clearances.
agentTrace.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.2 requires notice for work near 'high-voltage overhead lines' generally. The provided note specifically addresses transmission lines and references a transmission-specific contact. While a 48-hour notification concept is present, the note's limitation to transmission facilities does not fully satisfy the requirement to address all overhead distribution and transmission lines on or adjacent to the site.
